correctness.rationale: Exact affine generator identity yields every Apéry minimum, excluding larger coin totals by an explicit comparison. The +/-1 one-step Mersenne coin-length lemma confines possible isolated gaps to one residue, with exact zero-or-two test and Frobenius identification. Binary splitting and a no-carry bound prove the general Proth Hamming criterion for every n>=3, odd 1<=k<2^n. A separate Dijkstra vs dynamic-programming verifier checks 199 general semigroups, 68 Proth parameter pairs and 128 binary thresholds; finite tests supplement the unrestricted proof.

evidence: Moreno-Frías–Rosales establish structural covarieties and constructive algorithms for perfect semigroups at a fixed Frobenius number.
Singh–Ram explicitly restrict the isolated-gap formula to embedding-dimension-two numerical semigroups.
Srivastava–Thakkar address embedding dimensions broadly but detailed Apéry and Frobenius formulas are for k=2^r+1.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General algorithmic coverage of numerical semigroups does not constitute the new explicit infinite binary-weight classification. The two-generator case covers only occasional small instances; the Proth family has unbounded embedding dimension.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A prior theorem for binary-weight-two parameters does not entail the stated dependence on arbitrary popcounts, notably the infinitely many perfect cases such as k of weight three, or the all-m zero-or-two assertion. It would require the new generalized Apéry coin argument and binary splitting. The partial earlier special case is acknowledged rather than claimed new.

originality.rationale: Inspected Proth and isolated-gap primary literature provides Apéry structure for a special binary-weight-two parameter family, general criteria or bounded embedding-dimensional classifications, but does not imply a full all-k Hamming-weight dichotomy for the infinite Proth family. value.rationale: Determines whether every Proth semigroup is perfect and the exact isolated gaps by an explicit binary-weight criterion invariant under n; classifies an infinite family of unbounded embedding dimension, with a structural all-m theorem and an explicit Frobenius expression on the nonperfect branch. It extends the Proth invariant program and is not merely a routine numerical example.
